chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slanderer after the legal penalty has been established upon him, what is his repentance? He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should belie himself.' I said: 'What is your view if he belies himself and repents, would his testimony be accepted?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.'

key_terms.الْقَاذِفِ: The slanderer (one who accuses a chaste person of zina)

ai.seo_question: What is the repentance of a slanderer after receiving the hadd penalty, and is their testimony accepted?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the core of repentance for a slanderer (qadhf) lies in self-nullification—specifically, declaring the previous accusation false—which restores the validity of their testimony upon sincere repentance. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the legal disqualification (hudud) is lifted through this specific act of self-correction, emphasizing the restorative nature of tawbah in personal status matters. The emphasis on 'believing oneself' underscores the internal conviction required to validate the external legal standing.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinany who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the slanderer after the legal penalty (Hadd) having been established upon him, what is his repentance?’ Heasws said: ‘He should belie himself’. I said, ‘What is yourasws view if he belies himself and repents, would his testimony be accepted?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al-Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about an accuser who is convicted and subjected to penalty and about what his repentance is. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must call his soul a liar.’
I then asked, ‘If he calls his soul a liar and repents, is then his testimony acceptable ? 5 He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, it then becomes acceptable. 5 ”
